conviction_note: FY26 revenue and margin were pre-released on 14 Sep 2026 (rev GBP46-48m, adj. EBITDA margin 43-45%), so the move sits in the FY27 outlook and the Sep-30 order book. That is a scheduled guidance-type event on a thin AIM name, so abs_move is 7%. The evidence on its direction is balanced: an NED bought GBP138k at 690p after the year-end and the overhang seller (JPM) is finished, against a stock that has already retraced almost all of the warning (885p before, 862p now) with no RNS to explain it. p_up is therefore 49. The findings sum (+0.2) and the scaled number (-0.14) are both near zero and agree that there is no edge.

already_public.what: FY26 (to 30 Sep 2026) revenue estimated GBP46-48m and adjusted EBITDA margin 43-45%, against prior consensus of GBP52.8m and 45.2%. The miss was put down to delayed or deferred customer orders (licence expansions and upgrades). The company said 'back-order book remains strong'.
Canaccord Genuity cut its target from 2,060p to 1,760p. It sees FY26 revenue +2% and a return to growth in FY27 (10% revenue growth, modest margin expansion FY27-28), with net cash of GBP36m.
H1 FY26: new orders GBP39.6m, record back-order book GBP82.1m at 31 Mar 2026, net cash GBP32.5m, interim dividend +15% to 5.5p, pipeline GBP271m.
Results date confirmed for Monday 23 November; investor webinar 1 December.

new_in_release.expect: The FY27 outlook statement is the line that moves the stock. Cerillion gives a qualitative outlook against consensus. The direction depends on whether the deferred FY26 orders have closed since year-end. Unknown; there is no sourced evidence either way.

FY26 new orders and the back-order book at 30 Sep 2026. Likely above the GBP56.9m of a year earlier because of Omantel, and likely below March's GBP82.1m after H2 recognition on weak H2 intake. Probably framed as a record or near-record versus the prior year. Direction against expectations unknown.
FY26 revenue and margin inside the 14 Sep range. Expected to be no surprise.
Net cash about GBP36m per Canaccord. No reason to expect a surprise.
Final dividend probably raised (interim +15% despite profit -41%). Mildly positive and partly expected.

findings.finding: Non-executive director Guy O'Connor bought 20,000 shares (GBP138k) at 690p on 21 Oct 2026. That is three weeks after the 30 Sep year-end, when the board knew the FY26 outturn and early FY27 order flow, and just before the MAR closed period ahead of the 23 Nov results.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior insider-buy reaction measured. Outlook lines on results days moved the stock +7.0% (FY25 finals, 24 Nov 2025) and +1.3% (FY24 finals).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it has been public for a month and the stock is up about 25% from 690p since. What remains is the information content for the outlook statement itself. If that were fully in the price, the stock would already sit back above the pre-warning 885p.
findings.independence: none (the JPM exit below explains the price recovery, not the director's information)

findings.finding: The stock has retraced almost all of the September warning with no company news between: 885p before the warning, 774p on the day, a 660p low on 20 Oct, a run to 936p on 4-12 Nov, and 860p on 20 Nov. The only RNS in that window are the results-date notice and TR-1s. The outlook therefore has to deliver reassurance that is already partly paid for.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The two most recent outlook-sensitive releases were both sold: H1 trading update -5.6% (22 Apr 2026) and FY trading update -12.5% (14 Sep 2026). Interims fell -3.6% and -7.4% in 2026 and 2025.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself, so it is partly the free control (-run_up_20d, +23%). It is filed because the size of the retrace sets the bar for the outlook. If the market were demanding nothing, the stock would sit near the 700p post-warning level rather than within 3% of the pre-warning close.
findings.independence: Kalkine found no company-specific cause for the 4-11 Nov rises (https://kalkine.co.uk/news/technology/cerillion-plc-lsecer-slips-132-what-is-pressuring-the-shares, snippet only, 403 on fetch)

findings.finding: JPMorgan Asset Management cut its stake from 7.53% to 5.30% (9 Oct) and then below 5% (23 Oct 2026). The overhang seller after the warning finished just before the November rally, so less supply hangs over the results day.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior measurement on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the recovery since late October is the visible effect. The residual is the absence of a known large seller into any outlook disappointment.
findings.independence: Earlier step in the same disposal: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/cerillion--cer/tr-1-notification/9821054 (same holder, so not independent)

findings.finding: No contract-win RNS has been issued since the 8 Jan 2026 Omantel award, so between the 14 Sep warning and 20 Nov no single large deferred order (of the GBP17.3m Sep-2025 follow-on kind, which was RNS'd) has been announced as signed after the year-end.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Large contract RNSs moved the stock up sharply (Omantel +12% intraday on 8 Jan 2026, per AJ Bell).
findings.why_not_priced: The rally implies the market expects the slipped orders to be signing. The deferred items were licence expansions and upgrades, which Cerillion does not usually announce one by one, so this absence is weak evidence and is sized near zero.

findings.finding: The board raised the interim dividend 15% to 5.5p while H1 adjusted PBT fell 41%. That signals a progressive dividend held through the earnings dip, so a raised final dividend (last year 10.6p) is the likely line on the day.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The FY25 finals with a +17% total dividend rose 7.0%; the dividend's own share of that move is not separable.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly expected given the dividend history. The final dividend is a new line the market has not seen, and with net cash around GBP36m a step-up is affordable.

findings.finding: Delivery milestones since the warning support FY27 revenue recognition. Telesur's upgrade to Cerillion 26.1 went live on 28 Sep 2026, with a further Self Service phase to follow. The September update had already said Omantel software installation is complete and the UCom transformation is nearing completion.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Operational go-live RNSs have not been measured as movers on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly public. The residual is whether the release confirms the UCom cutover and quantifies FY27 recognition from the back-order book.

outside_window.finding: The online investor presentation with Q&A on 1 Dec 2026 is after the one-session window.

baseline_tension: The lean is flat (+0.08), and the 20d run-up (+23%) argues against the stock as a free control. My findings agree with neither side strongly: the insider buy and the finished seller lean up, the retrace leans down, and the net is about zero.
language_note: nothing the English sources did not already carry: the domestic RNS record (Investegate) supplied the primary documents, namely the 14 Sep pre-release with the GBP52.8m prior consensus, the NED purchase and the JPM TR-1s. The international and wire coverage (Sharecast via HL, AskTraders) restated those and added only Canaccord's FY27 view.
lessons_applied: 'The move is in the guide' (a first outlook for a new fiscal year is a scheduled guidance event): abs_move_pct raised from 6.0 to 7.0, because the FY27 outlook against a single-broker bar is the line on the day.
'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0': the delivery-milestones finding cut from +0.3 to +0.1, since Omantel and UCom status were already in the 14 Sep RNS.
'The drawdown has no cause in the filings is worth 0; in a small cap the filing record is not the information set': the no-contract-RNS absence finding cut from -0.5 to -0.2.
p_up unchanged at 49: pre-released period, no sourced unseen number.
